mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC fell to a trough at t-2w (-37.3) and has since improved for two consecutive weeks to -34.3, indicating a self-reinforcing recovery in shopping and recreation activity that should continue over the near term.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -37.3 at t-2w to -34.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days despite two prior weeks of consecutive improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility above a threshold signals a behavioral substitution where households redirect leisure time outdoors (parks, trails) instead of indoor retail and recreation venues, depressing RETAIL_REC over the following month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 2 points week-on-week for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS increased from 6.6 at t-2w to 11.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even as PARKS continues to climb beyond the trigger threshold, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the last two weeks reflects renewed commuting routines that generate incidental retail footfall near transit hubs and office districts, jointly lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -41.6 to -34.4 and TRANSIT improved from -33.6 to -28.0 over t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 14 days even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue their joint upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: Stable, low RESIDENTIAL values combined with rising PARKS across four weeks are consistent with a summer reopening regime in which households spend less time at home and more time out, supporting a continued gradual rise in retail and recreation mobility.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed in a narrow 5.4-6.0 band while PARKS rose from 9.4 to 11.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining flat and PARKS continuing to rise, breaking the assumed seasonal linkage.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility deteriorates below a caution threshold, it signals renewed household risk-aversion or essential-only shopping behavior that spills over into reduced discretionary retail and recreation visits.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -28 for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached -28.1 at t-2w before partially recovering to -24.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 14 days even if GROCERY_PHARM crosses below -28 for two straight weeks, invalidating the spillover claim.

mechanism_narrative: Consistently low and stable RESIDENTIAL values indicate that people are not retreating to home-centric routines, which structurally supports sustained or rising out-of-home retail and recreation activity over the coming month.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 5.4 and 6.0 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains flat or decreases, showing no structural link between home-staying behavior and retail mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PARKS and flat RESIDENTIAL during warm-season months suggests households are reallocating leisure time toward outdoor parks rather than indoor retail venues, an interaction that should suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the next month if both conditions persist together.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose to 11.9 while RESIDENTIAL held near 5.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even as PARKS keeps climbing and RESIDENTIAL stays flat, contradicting the proposed substitution interaction.

mechanism_narrative: In the absence of any sharp week-on-week deterioration across WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, or RESIDENTIAL that would signal new restrictions, the current steady-state policy regime implies continuity of the mild recovery trend already visible in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:No series shows a sudden multi-week deterioration consistent with new restrictions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 7 days despite no observable deterioration in WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, or RESIDENTIAL, indicating the policy-stability assumption does not hold.
